methods.description: Read ones/tenths/hundredths/thousandths and state each digit’s value or write the standard sum. Omit zero-value terms while preserving their positions in the written decimal; use the same place reading to correct a misplaced digit.

Combine stated parts by placing their values in the correct columns. Read their total as a decimal or check that two partitions have the same total. Combining is the reverse of the source partition equality, not a new general decimal arithmetic algorithm.

Combine or redistribute place-value parts without changing the total, including collecting decimal places into one part and moving one whole into decimal parts. Check requested constraints such as the first part, exactly two decimal parts, or three non-zero parts none equal to a standard part. An elementary adaptation of the actual grouped5ones+429thousandths context; no original filled constrained example is claimed.

Write/read the full partition and compare the given known parts with it. Find the leftover value or read the requested missing digit once the represented decimal is known. Keep decimal place positions aligned; no algebra or general column subtraction procedure is needed.
